Forward algorithm for hidden semi-Markov models

forward_hsmm.Rd

Calculates the (approximate) log-likelihood of a sequence of observations under a hidden semi-Markov model using a modified forward algorithm. Dwell-time distributions and conditional transition probabilities can be fixed, track-specific, time-varying or periodic.

Usage

forward_hsmm(
  dm,
  omega,
  allprobs,
  trackID = NULL,
  delta = NULL,
  eps = 1e-10,
  report = TRUE,
  tod = NULL,
  use_all_obs = FALSE,
  first_obs = NULL,
  logspace = FALSE
)

Arguments

dm

list of length nStates containing the dwell-time probability mass functions (PMFs) of the states, where each element is either

  • a vector, if the dwell-time distribution is fixed, or

  • a matrix with nTracks rows (track-specific), nObs rows (time-varying), or L rows (periodic, if tod is provided), where each row is a PMF.

The vector lengths or numbers of columns correspond to the approximating state aggregate sizes, hence there should be little probability mass not covered by these.

omega

matrix of dimension c(nStates, nStates) of conditional transition probabilities, also called embedded transition probability matrix, or array with nTracks, nObs or L of such matrices as slices.

Contains the transition probabilities given that the current state is left. Hence, the diagonal elements need to be zero and the rows need to sum to one. Can be constructed using tpm_switch.

allprobs

matrix of state-dependent probabilities/ density values of dimension c(nObs, nStates) which will automatically be converted to the appropriate dimension.

trackID

optional vector of length nObs containing IDs

If provided, the total log-likelihood will be the sum of each track's likelihood contribution. In this case, dm and omega can be track-specific and delta can be a matrix of initial distributions, of dimension c(nTracks, nStates), such that each track starts with its own initial distribution.

delta

optional vector of initial state probabilities of length nStates, in which case a new stay begins at the first observation used in each track.

By default, the stationary distribution is computed (which is typically recommended).

eps

small value to avoid numerical issues in the approximating transition matrix construction. Usually, this should not be changed.

report

logical, indicating whether initial distribution, dm, omega and the allprobs matrix should be reported from the fitted model. Defaults to TRUE.

tod

optional integer vector of length nObs containing the time of day (or any other cycle), with values in 1, ..., L, for periodic models.

With periodic dm, it needs to advance by one in each row within a track.

use_all_obs

logical, only relevant for time-varying dm.

By default, the first max(sapply(dm, ncol)) - 1 observations of each track are not used, as they may belong to stays that began before the first observation, with unknown dwell-time distributions. If TRUE, all observations are used, which needs delta.

first_obs

optional integer, the first observation that is used in each track.

By default 1, or max(sapply(dm, ncol)) for time-varying dm, in which case it cannot be smaller. Useful to fit models with different aggregate sizes or types of dm to the same observations, such that their likelihoods can be compared.

logspace

logical, indicating whether allprobs contains log-probabilities. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

HSMM log-likelihood for given data and parameters

Details

Hidden semi-Markov models (HSMMs) are a flexible extension of HMMs, where the state duration distribution is explicitly modelled by a distribution on the positive integers. For direct numerical maximum likelihood estimation, HSMMs can be represented as HMMs on an enlarged state space (of size \(M\)) and with structured transition probabilities.

A stay that begins at time point t is governed by omega[,,t] (which state is entered) and row t of dm (how long the stay lasts).

This function is designed to be used with automatic differentiation based on the R package RTMB. It will be very slow without it!

References

Langrock, R., & Zucchini, W. (2011). Hidden Markov models with arbitrary state dwell-time distributions. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 55(1), 715-724.

Koslik, J. O. (2025). Hidden semi-Markov models with inhomogeneous state dwell-time distributions. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 209, 108171.

See also

Other forward algorithms: forward(), forward_g(), forward_ihsmm(), forward_p(), forward_phsmm()

Examples

## negative log-likelihood of a 2-state HSMM with shifted Poisson dwell times
nll = function(par) {
  getAll(par)
  sizes = c(20, 20) # state aggregate sizes
  dm = lapply(1:2, function(i) dpois(1:sizes[i] - 1, exp(loglambda[i])))
  omega = matrix(c(0, 1, 1, 0), 2) # 2 states: no parameters
  allprobs = matrix(1, length(step), 2)
  ind = which(!is.na(step))
  for(j in 1:2) allprobs[ind, j] = dgamma2(step[ind], exp(logmu[j]), exp(logsigma[j]))
  -forward_hsmm(dm, omega, allprobs)
}
step = trex$step[1:200]
par = list(loglambda = log(c(5, 5)), logmu = log(c(0.3, 2.5)), logsigma = log(c(0.2, 1.5)))
obj = MakeADFun(nll, par, silent = TRUE)
opt = nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
